content.text: Found it — the CSV headers are `Latitude`, `Longitude`, `Magnitude` (capitalized), but the `/position-accessor` node uses `[d.longitude, d.latitude]` (lowercase). Since `FileOp` parses the CSV with `d3.csv`, field names keep their original case, so `d.longitude`/`d.latitude` are always `undefined`, producing `NaN` positions for every point — hence a blank map. The `/magnitude-accessor` node correctly uses `d.Magnitude` (capital M), which is what tipped this off as a case-mismatch bug rather than a broader wiring issue.

content.text: Test environment requires a Playwright browser that isn't installed here — unrelated to the fix. Let's just confirm the JSON itself is still valid.

The JSON is still valid; the test failure is an unrelated Playwright browser-install issue in this environment, not something caused by the edit.

## What was wrong

The `/position-accessor` node (an `AccessorOp`) used the expression `[d.longitude, d.latitude]` to compute each point's map position, but `data.csv`'s headers are capitalized: `Latitude`, `Longitude` (along with `Magnitude`, etc.). Since `FileOp` parses CSVs via `d3.csv`/`d3.autoType`, column names keep their exact case, so `d.longitude` and `d.latitude` were always `undefined` — every point got an invalid `[undefined, undefined]` position, so nothing rendered on the map.

Interestingly, the `/magnitude-accessor` node right next to it correctly used `d.Magnitude` (capital M), which made the case-sensitivity mismatch on the position accessor the clear culprit.

## Fix

Changed the position accessor expression to match the actual CSV column casing:

```json
"expression": "[d.Longitude, d.Latitude]"
```

No other case mismatches were found elsewhere in the graph.
